chapter: Fred Astaire and the high points
title: Baker's Keyboard Lounge pays more and limits him to twenty-minute sets
summary: The Detroit club owner who once refused him now paid Burke double and held him to 20-minute sets so hustlers kept buying champagne, while Burke made difficult clubs pay.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: But now I'm in Detroit. Now, the guy was always telling him "Don't call me about Jonah," out at Baker's. This guy calls Sammy and Sammy laid it on him. Sammy laid the bread on him. "Well, I tried to get you to take him last year again, and you said no, so now it will cost you twice as much. If not, we've got other places to go. The records are jumping." Had a big following there. So we went in for him, at Baker's, and he's got lines up in the snow, on both sides of the street, and he's making us cut the session down to 20 minutes, and says, "You can only stay one set and you have to pay again."

That's the only way he could make any money, because Sammy had charged him all this bread, and the guy -- we'd get up there and do 20 minutes, which was about two numbers. You know, we'd play one number and then play a long one, a show number, and off.
Well, what kind of cover was he charging?
Huh? Oh, he was charging like -- I think he was charging 2.50, and they'd say in there about 20 minutes, 25 at the most, and I stayed up there 25, he'd come back and
argue, he'd say, "Jonah, cut it down now. It was 25 minutes. Cut it down."
I'll bet he had some griping there.

Oh, man, what griping he had, you know, because he had all the hustlers and things come up from John A. Street, at that hotel out there, the Gotham. They would come out and buy champagne, you know. They didn't care what it was. They just stayed all night anyway. No used to talk to them about going after the one set. When they started doing that it didn't do us no good either, because some of the people wondered, "What's going on, Jonah? Stay up there." I'd say, "Well, this is orders from the boss. You have to ask him."
So this went on -- then we started going back regular then, you know, and charging him too. Sammy charged him, to make him pay. "I'm going to make him pay, because of how he was before."
For saying he didn't want you back.

Yeah, uh-huh. He said, "I'm going to make him pay." So the people that was good to us, he said, "We're going to be good to them. The people that was hard to get along with, we're going to make them pay." So the guy at the Theatrical, we never did make him go up where he should. And we just went out there this year for him, you know. Not as I like the room, but --
